hero.lead: Four island states and 114,000 people across the western Pacific, with $3.3 billion of United States economic assistance through 2043 under the renewed Compact and forest over nine tenths of the land.

register.name: Compact Trust Fund of the Federated States of Micronesia
register.detail: Balance $1.98 billion at 30 November 2025 (Trust Fund Committee) · United States contributions of $500 million made available by the end of FY2025 under the amended Compact · No withdrawals made or planned as of January 2026
register.note: IMF, January 2026: the assets of the Compact and FSM trust funds reached a combined 508% of GDP
register.text: The trust fund set up under the Compact of Free Association and built with United States contributions, the largest financial reserve of the Federated States of Micronesia. It is a long-term reserve for the public finances as a whole; as of January 2026 no withdrawals had been made or planned.
by: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia

register.name: WHO grant for health priorities, 2026–2027 biennium
register.detail: World Health Organization · extended 19 January 2026 · FSM health priority activities for the 2026–2027 biennium budget · Congressional Resolution No. 24-137
register.note: Resolution to approve and accept the grant introduced in the Congress of the FSM on 30 June 2026
register.text: A grant of $5,520,000 from the World Health Organization for the health priority activities of the Federated States of Micronesia in the 2026–2027 biennium. It finances the health standard directly.

register.name: Increasing resilience to the health risks of climate change (SAP051)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · Approved 3 July 2025 (B.42) · Grant · Accredited entity: the Pacific Community (SPC) · Funded activity agreement effective 9 June 2026 · Completion 9 June 2031 · Total value $18.8 million
register.note: Accepted by the Congress of the FSM on 15 August 2025 (Congressional Resolution No. 24-47)
register.text: A $17.9 million Green Climate Fund grant, through the Pacific Community, for climate-induced disease prevention and early warning of climate-sensitive diseases in Micronesia. It strengthens climate-health policies and systems and community resilience to climate-related health risks: the health standard.

register.name: Access and Renewable Increase for Sustainable Energy (ARISE)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · IDA grant of SDR 32.3 million · Financing agreement April 2025 · Launched 28 May 2025 · Chuuk, Pohnpei, Yap and Kosrae
register.note: Electricity for over 3,500 people in remote outer islands
register.text: A US$42 million World Bank project for solar-powered mini grids and stand-alone solar home systems on four unelectrified islands in Chuuk, new grid-connected solar and battery storage in Chuuk and Pohnpei, and grid resilience upgrades in Pohnpei, Yap and Kosrae. It finances the energy standard, bringing electricity to more than 3,500 people in the remote outer islands.

register.name: Strengthening Public Financial Management II
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 5 March 2025 · IDA grant of SDR 9.9 million (US$13 million equivalent) · Grant award 10 March 2025 · Accepted by the Congress of the FSM 14 August 2025
register.text: A US$13 million IDA grant to expand the fiscal management information systems of the Federated States of Micronesia, improve procurement, set up an internal audit function and train local finance staff. It strengthens the public finances as a whole, which the World Bank links to better delivery of healthcare, education and infrastructure.

register.name: Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program, second phase (FSM PROPER)
register.text: The second phase of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program in Micronesia, for economic resilience. It finances sustainable fisheries and the ocean economy, a source of food and livelihood for the islands.

register.name: Climate change adaptation solutions for local authorities (FP169)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · Approved 7 October 2021 · Grant · Accredited entity: the Pacific Community (SPC) · Effective 20 October 2021 · Completion 20 October 2028 · 18% of GCF financing disbursed
register.text: A $16.6 million Green Climate Fund grant that builds the capacity of local authorities in Micronesia to deliver climate change adaptation services. It covers food and water security, disaster risk reduction and recovery, and community climate resilience: the food and water standards.

register.name: Grant to ease the fuel price shock (Crisis Response Plan)
register.detail: ADB · Approved 23 October 2026 · Asian Development Fund grant through the Countercyclical Support Facility · 28% of the government’s projected $20 million financing gap
register.note: Cash assistance aims to reach at least 29,000 people, identified through the national social registry
register.text: A $5.6 million ADB grant toward the government’s $20 million Crisis Response Plan, which includes a $15 million Fuel Stabilization Fund to cushion sharp fuel price increases. It keeps essential public services running and finances temporary cash assistance for vulnerable households: the public finances, energy and livelihood.

register.name: FSMDB Increasing Access to Finance for SMEs
register.detail: ADB · Signed 18 August 2026 · $4 million loan from ordinary capital resources · Reimbursable grant of up to $1 million from the Asian Development Fund private sector window (ADB Wayfinder (Pacific) Program) · Borrower: FSM Development Bank
register.note: ADB’s first private sector project in the FSM; at least 50% of financing for women-led SMEs
register.text: A $5 million ADB financing package with the Federated States of Micronesia Development Bank, a national government-affiliated development financial institution, to scale lending to underserved small businesses nationwide. At least half goes to women-led small and medium-sized enterprises, with training for at least 250 of them and a women-focused financial product: the livelihood standard.

register.name: Typhoon Sinlaku emergency response grant
register.detail: ADB · 4 June 2026 · Asia Pacific Disaster Response Fund · Grant 1109-FSM · Chuuk and Yap
register.note: A fast-tracked grant for emergency and humanitarian efforts
register.text: A $500,000 grant from ADB’s Asia Pacific Disaster Response Fund to the Government of the Federated States of Micronesia after Typhoon Sinlaku. It finances emergency and humanitarian relief for the urgent needs of people in Chuuk and Yap states.

register.name: FSM Immunization and Vaccines for Children Program
register.detail: United States, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention · Grant award 24 June 2026 · Budget period 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 · Accepted by the Congress of the FSM 6 July 2026 (Congressional Resolution No. 24-149)
register.text: A grant from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, for the national immunization and vaccines for children programme. It finances the health standard.
by: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

register.name: Climate resilience package: school water and sanitation, evacuation shelters
register.detail: Australian Government · 24 March 2026 · from within the existing bilateral development budget · Safe drinking water and basic sanitation in schools · Upgrades to emergency evacuation shelters
register.note: Total Australian ODA to the FSM: A$11.4 million, budget estimate for 2025–26
register.text: A $2.5 million Australian package for climate resilience in Micronesia, from within the existing bilateral development budget. It finances safe drinking water and basic sanitation for girls and children with disabilities in schools, and upgrades to emergency evacuation shelters: the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Project for Strengthening Maternal Health Care Services at Primary Service Delivery Points
register.detail: Government of Japan · Exchange of Notes signed 18 February 2026 · Grant assistance of up to 533 million yen · Implemented with UNFPA
register.note: About $3.4 million, according to the Embassy of Japan
register.text: Japanese grant assistance of up to 533 million yen to improve obstetrics and gynaecology facilities, install medical equipment, build waiting facilities for pregnant and postpartum women in remote areas and train health workers in each state. It aims to widen equitable access to maternal health care and lower maternal mortality: the health standard.

register.name: Strengthening the Public Health Infrastructure, Workforce and Data System
register.detail: United States, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention · Component A · Notice of award 2 December 2025 · Accepted by the Congress of the FSM 23 January 2026 (Congressional Resolution No. 24-107)
register.text: A grant from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, to strengthen the public health infrastructure, workforce and data system of the Federated States of Micronesia. It finances the health standard.
by: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

register.name: Goods and Services Program for the FSM: fisheries development
register.detail: Government of Japan · Extended 17 September 2025 under a Memorandum of Understanding · Accepted by the Congress of the FSM 22 May 2026 (Congressional Resolution No. 24-86)
register.text: A Japanese grant of $300,000 under the Goods and Services Program for the FSM, to assist the fisheries development programme. It supports fisheries, a source of food and livelihood for the islands.

register.name: Compact of Free Association, economic assistance
register.detail: United States · Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-42) · Signed 9 March 2024 · Through FY2043 · Sector grants of $140 million a year · $140 million allocated for FY2027 (12 November 2026)
register.note: All three nations: $6.5 billion of assistance (U.S. Department of the Interior); sector grants are 85% of the Micronesia total
register.text: Twenty years of United States economic assistance to Micronesia under the renewed Compact, in sector grants and contributions to the Compact Trust Fund. Compact health and education grants fund nearly all annual operating costs of those services; in FY2025 Micronesia planned $86.1 million, 62% of its sector grants, for health and education.
